newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.S. and EU agree to combat prostitution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. and EU agree to combat prostitution.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and leaders of the European Union agreed on Wednesday to step up efforts to combat a rise in prostitution, which Clinton likened to "modern day slavery".

"Today we agreed to intensify our cooperation against a new problem that we face, the increasing practice of trafficking in women," Clinton said after talks in the Dutch capital with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and European Commission President Jacques Santer.

The problem "recreates in an entirely different context almost a new kind of modern day slavery. And we intend to do what we can to stop it," said Clinton, whose visit to the Netherlands also included a celebration of the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan for the rebuilding of Europe after World War Two.

A senior U.S. official who briefed reporters after the semi-annual U.S.-EU summit said that organised crime groups in Russia and Central Europe were "running what in effect are prostitution rings" in western Europe and parts of Asia.
"The same rackets that are involved in this are often also involved in drug trafficking and arms smuggling," deputy U.S. National Security Adviser James Steinberg said.

Steinberg said Clinton and E.U. leaders were committed to exchange information on the problem in order to have a better understanding of how to combat it and help central and eastern European countries strengthen their law enforcement.
